name: Makkai ki Roti
instructions: 1. In a large bowl, mix the maize flour, salt, and carom seeds. 2. Gradually add warm water to the flour, kneading it into a soft and pliable dough. 3. Divide the dough into equal-sized balls. 4. Flatten the ball between your palms or on a plastic sheet, as maize dough is fragile and lacks gluten. 5. Heat a tawa (griddle) and place the flattened roti on it. 6. Cook on medium heat, flipping until both sides develop golden brown spots. 7. Apply a generous amount of ghee and serve hot.
description: Makkai ki Roti is a staple comfort food in the rural households of Himachal Pradesh. During the harvest season, this wholesome bread provides essential warmth and energy to locals, typically paired with Sarson ka Saag or locally grown legumes, reflecting the agrarian traditions of the Himalayan belt.
